description.narrative: The United Nations Development Program’s (UNDP) ‘’Democracy Strengthening in Zambia (DSZ) project’’ is a three-year multi-donor project designed to address recently identified evolving challenges and builds on previous electoral interventions as Zambia enters its next electoral cycle and the run-up to general elections in 2021

UNDPs ''Democracy Strengthening in Zambia (DSZ) project '' är en treårig insats som stöds av flera givare. Insatsen har utformats för att hantera utmaningar kopplade till de allmänna valen i Zambia 2021 och bygger på erfarenheter från tidigare liknande valinterventioner.

The overall Goal of the project is that Zambia has strengthened democracy through functional and inclusive electoral processes that ensure the peaceful conduct of the 2021 elections and demonstrate heightened legitimacy and institutionalization of the multiparty system. The DSZ consists of two interlinked result areas: (1) electoral institutions and processes strengthened and (2) programming for peace in support of the Zambian electoral cycle. These two result areas are strongly interlinked with following six key results:1. Inclusive and participatory decision-making;2. Strengthened, responsive and accountable institutions;3. Transparent institutions with improved access to information;4. Improved technical and organizational capacities of national electoral stakeholders;5. Credible and legitimate institutions work with integrity, and6. Enhanced conflict prevention and mitigation mechanisms.

Below some milestone achievements as per the 2024 UNDP DSZ Annual Report.
Support Inclusion Measures of the National Assembly Dialogue Meetings held in 10 of 20 targeted women led constituencies with engaged bipartisan stakeholders from UPND and PF, political leaders, CSOs, traditional and religious authorities, and media. The meetings identified barriers to inclusive political participation, commitments to gender sensitive policies, and awareness programs. Traditional and religious leaders pledged to champion inclusivity and anti gender based violence initiatives.
Zambia Electoral Stakeholders Conference (ZESC) The first of its kind (ZESC) was held from 2729 November 2024, coinciding with Zambia's 60th independence anniversary, and with 160 attendees from government, political parties, CSOs, media, academia, and international partners. Topics included: Enhancing citizen participation, electoral integrity, addressing malpractices, violence, and civic space infringements. Key presentations on electoral reforms, information integrity, cost of elections, technological adaptation, and governance frameworks.
Strengthening Parliamentary Committees and Staff Governance related training for parliamentary committee members and technical staff were held to improve legislative reviews, organization of committee sessions, and quicker response times.
Post Legislative Scrutiny (PLS) Training was held for parliamentarians and staff. The training enhanced understanding of PLS principles, leading to more effective legislative decisions.
Support to the Judiciarys Advisory Committee on Election Management The Strategic Plan was approved, providing a framework for election dispute resolution. Reviews of Election Dispute Resolution (EDR) cases was done which identified trends and gaps to improve efficiency, transparency, and fairness in handling electoral disputes.
Support for National Assembly Communication Strategy A parlamentary reporting workshop was held with 36 journalists to enhance media coverage and parliamentary reporting. Democracy Dialogue Series Eight episodes to to educate the public and increase voter participation. The launch event focused on information integrity and elections. A panel discussion on media polarization, misinformation, and AI in electoral narratives was held.
Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Policy (GESIP) The policy was approved by ECZ, with an aim to integrate inclusive practices in electoral processes. The focus is on representation of women, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups.
Training for ECZ Staff Staff was trained to improved understanding of electoral management. Knowledge comprehension increased from 55% to 85%, enhancing election management skills.
Electoral Reforms and Public Participation The Electoral Reforms Technical Committee (ETRC) was launched on July 19, 2024, with 30 members from key institutions. Public consultations were conducted across all ten provinces, generating 1,367 submissions, including significant input from youth (10.6%) and persons with disabilities (3.5%). The ERCT Report was publicized on June 3rd 2025.
Political Party Regulatory Framework An MoU was signed between Zambia Center for Interparty Dialogue (ZCID) and Transparency International Zambia on March 26, 2024. Seven groups were formed to review political party regulations, focusing on registration, funding, campaign financing, inclusion, and enforcement.
Public Events Management System (PEMS) PEMS were installed in 22 police stations across five provinces, which enhanced efficiency, coordination, and realtime data access for the Zambia Police Service (ZPS).
Zambia Police Communication Strategy A first ever communications strategy to improve communication and public relations was adopted by ZPS.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
